## Git cheat sheet

```bash
# --- daily loop ---
git status                       # what's changed?
git switch -c feature/thing      # new branch + move to it
git add .                        # stage everything
git commit -m "Describe change"  # save a snapshot
git switch main                  # back to main
git pull                         # get latest from GitHub
git log --oneline                # history

# --- undo (safe) ---
git restore <file>               # discard un-staged changes to a file
git restore --staged <file>      # unstage (keep the edit)
git switch -                     # jump back to previous branch

# --- undo (careful — ask first) ---
git reset --hard <commit>        # DESTRUCTIVE: discards work
git push --force                 # DESTRUCTIVE on shared branches
git clean -fd                    # DESTRUCTIVE: deletes untracked files
```

## GitHub (`gh`) cheat sheet

```bash
gh auth login                    # sign in (once)
gh auth status                   # am I logged in?
gh repo create NAME --private --source=. --push   # repo from current folder
git push -u origin BRANCH        # push a branch
gh pr create --fill              # open a PR (auto title/body from commits)
gh pr create --title "T" --body "B"
gh pr diff                       # REVIEW the change — do this before merging
gh pr merge --squash --delete-branch   # merge and tidy up
gh repo delete NAME --yes        # delete a throwaway repo
```

## Claude Code cheat sheet

```bash
claude                           # start a session in the current folder
claude --version                 # check it's installed
```

Inside a session, useful things to say:

| Say this | To… |
|----------|-----|
| "Before editing, tell me your plan and which files you'll change." | Get plan-then-act |
| "Show me the diff." / "Run the tests." | Force it to show its work |
| "Make a branch called `x` and work there." | Keep it off `main` |
| "Commit this with a clear message." | Delegate the git mechanics |
| "Push and open a PR into main." | Delegate the PR |
| "Start over" / open a new session | Clear a confused/overlong context |

::: {.callout-tip}
## When an agent gets confused
Nine times out of ten the fix is one of: **(1)** start a fresh session (clean context), **(2)** give a more specific prompt with file paths, or **(3)** break the task into smaller steps.
:::

## Glossary {#glossary}

| Term | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| **Agent** | An LLM that can use tools (read/write files, run code, search) in a loop to complete tasks. |
| **Agentic loop** | Act → observe result → decide next action → repeat, until done or it needs you. |
| **Branch** | A parallel line of work in git; a sandbox that doesn't touch `main`. |
| **`CLAUDE.md`** | A project (or global) file of standing instructions an agent reads each session. |
| **Commit** | A saved snapshot of your files in git, with a message. |
| **Context window** | How much text (files, instructions, conversation) the model can "see" at once. |
| **Diff** | The line-by-line difference between two versions — your review surface. |
| **`gh`** | The GitHub command-line tool, used for auth and pull requests. |
| **Hallucination** | A plausible-but-false statement from a model; the reason we verify. |
| **LLM** | Large language model — the model underneath the agent. |
| **MCP** | Model Context Protocol — a standard for giving agents extra tools/data sources. |
| **Merge** | Combining an approved branch into `main`; your explicit "keep this." |
| **Prompt** | What you ask the agent (and the skill of asking well). |
| **Pull request (PR)** | A proposal on GitHub to merge a branch, with a reviewable diff. |
| **Repository (repo)** | A folder tracked by git. |
| **Skill** | A reusable, packaged procedure for a recurring task. |
| **Token** | The unit LLMs read/write text in (~¾ of a word); measures context and cost. |
| **Workflow** | A repeatable multi-step process, assembled from `CLAUDE.md` + skills + the git loop. |

## After today
The best next step is *usage*: pick one real repo, add a `CLAUDE.md`, and start running the branch → PR → merge loop with an agent. Grow your skills folder each time you catch yourself re-explaining something.
:::
